AI vendors
Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter are used only by Fly.io’s internal tooling, under our AI usage policy. We never send the contents of your volumes, or the bodies of requests to your applications, to an AI vendor. OpenRouter routes a request to a third-party model provider; our policy limits its internal use to providers whose terms prohibit training on the content, and OpenRouter itself does not train on inputs or outputs.
During support and abuse investigations, the data that can be processed is account and organization metadata, support ticket text, and platform log lines, which include whatever your application writes to stdout. For Managed Postgres, our support tooling can also process a cluster’s Postgres logs and, when a Fly.io operator runs a read-only diagnostic query during an investigation, the results of that query.
Changes
Additions to and removals from this list are recorded here. Under section 6.3 of our Data Processing Agreement, a new or replacement sub-processor is listed here at least 30 days before it processes customer personal data, this page is the notice of that appointment, and objections on data protection grounds may be sent to compliance@fly.io within 10 days of the listing.
2026-10-29: Added Hivelocity and Zenlayer. Neither processes customer personal data before 2026-11-28.
2026-10-24: Added ClickHouse and OpenRouter. Neither processes customer personal data before 2026-11-23.
2026-09-24: Added Dropbox Sign, incident.io, and Vultr.
2026-05-18: Removed Equinix and OVH.
